A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the circumstellar disk properties of WTTSs are a continuum of those observed for CTTSs and that the disk frequency of WTTSs is a function of age and location within a molecular cloud.
the circumstellar disk lifetimes are not a simple function of the age of the star.
the circumstellar dust disks around WTTSs have lifetimes of ~1 Myrs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
circumstellar disks of WTTSs are common, but they are not ubiquitous.
the disk fractions of WTTSs are strongly dependent on the location of the stars in the H-R diagrams and that the disk dissipation timescale for the youngest WTTSs may be as short as ~1 Myr.

the timescale for circumstellar disk dissipation is shorter than the age spread of WTTSs, and thus that the timescale of planet formation is likely to be shorter than the age dispersion of the WTTS population.
